subject.title: [Bug]: Browser interactions can exhaust model context by injecting too much page content

question: Should OpenClaw make compact, goal-shaped browser reads the default behavior, and if so what explicit raw/full escape hatch should remain for workflows that need complete page state?
rationale: Current main has caps and an efficient mode, but turning this into the default model-facing browser behavior changes the browser tool contract and needs owner intent before an automated repair chooses semantics.

options.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
options.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable, keep explicit full/raw AI/ARIA reads for workflows that need complete refs, and validate both paths with browser plugin tests and live proof.

options.title: Keep opt-in efficient mode
options.body: Leave current defaults mostly intact and document when agents should use mode=efficient, maxChars, selector reads, and generic pruning for context-heavy browser workflows.

options.title: Track under broader browser roadmap
options.body: Close this specific direction into the broader browser field report only if maintainers want a single umbrella to own action diffs, stale refs, viewport reads, and context shaping together.

recommendation.title: Compact default with raw escape hatch
recommendation.body: Make the default snapshot/read path compact and actionable, keep explicit full/raw AI/ARIA reads for workflows that need complete refs, and validate both paths with browser plugin tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Browser snapshot modes and bundled browser ownership history make this the best available product-boundary owner signal.
